name: Wildlife and Habitat Program Grants
summary: Grants of up to $20,000 to organisations headquartered in Alaska, Idaho, Montana, Oregon or Washington for work preserving wildlife and habitat, including landscape connectivity and freshwater and marine biodiversity. Open cycles run in spring.

geography.label: Alaska, Idaho, Montana, Oregon and Washington

reporting: Final report describing how the funds were spent

eligibility.rule: Headquartered in Washington, Oregon, Idaho, Montana or Alaska, and the program runs there
Received formal-application grants in fewer than 3 of the last 5 years, excluding invitational and discretionary grants
Mission statement includes wildlife and habitat preservation
Project does not take place primarily in urban areas
Project excludes wildlife rehabilitation and captive breeding
Project does not preserve small isolated parcels or land valued solely for recreation
Project is not for a city park, zoo or aquarium

eligibility.quote: We define the Western States as Washington, Oregon, Idaho, Montana, and Alaska. To be eligible for funding, organizations must be headquartered in this region, and the proposed programs must take place within this region.

However, we request that you not reapply if you have received funding from the Foundation through our formal application process in 3 or more out of the most recent 5 years. Invitational and discretionary grants are exempt from this limit.
Organizations whose mission statement does not include wildlife and habitat preservation
Preserving of small isolated parcels of land Preservation of land solely valued for recreational purposes
